story: As the hazy October evening settles over Sumter Oaks at 7:17, Gary is making his way to Magnolia Loop with a determined stride, while Donna, upbeat as ever, heads toward the Rec Center. Hal stays put on his porch, content in his chair and keeping a casual eye on the street as he weighs which chair to haul over to Rosa's on Saturday. Rosa, equally determined, is off to Town Square, the two of them crossing paths in the golden gloom of the community's quiet evening.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal waited: Settling into the porch chair as the haze thickens, keeping a casual eye on Magnolia Loop and thinking about which chair to haul over to Rosa's on Saturday.

gary.thought_process: I'm in Town Square with nobody around, and I already signed up for the parade last tick, so there's nothing more to do at the signup table. My cart modification request is still pending at Architectural Review, and L-01 says I can't mess with the exterior until that's approved. The lights and speakers can't go on the street-facing parts yet, but I can sort out the wiring plan and parts list at home, and I need a clean shirt and Late Wife's baked beans ready for Rosa's Saturday dinner anyway. Quiet hours start at 10 PM, so no sound system testing late. Best use of this hour is heading back to Magnolia Loop to work in the garage on the interior wiring and test the lights.

parameters.content: Heading home to the garage to work out the wiring plan and parts list while Architectural Review makes up its mind.

donna.thought_process: Rosa is heading off to shop and the flamingo issue is settled at three. She already has my dessert answer, lemon bars, so I shouldn't repeat myself. The ladder sign-up is done and Gary is on board. I should keep my goal moving, so I'll head to the rec center to see about court time for doubles practice with Gary before Saturday's dinner. That keeps the pickleball plan alive without rehashing the dinner chat.

parameters.content: Heading to the rec center to look at court time for doubles practice with Gary.

hal.thought_process: Notebook's been reviewed twice already and the open entries are settled. Nobody's in sight, the street is quiet, and I've repeated the same porch-sitting routine for a few ticks now. Saturday at Rosa's is the thing that matters, and I promised a sturdy chair and clean boots. No point sitting here stewing. I'll wait out the evening haze and keep an eye on the loop out of habit, without making a production of it.

parameters.content: Settling into the porch chair as the haze thickens, keeping a casual eye on Magnolia Loop and thinking about which chair to haul over to Rosa's on Saturday.

rosa.thought_process: Donna has the dessert covered with lemon bars, Gary is confirmed, and Hal is already helping. Everything I needed from Donna is settled, and asking again would just be repeating myself. It's 7:17 PM and the stores are probably still open, so the useful thing is to stop chatting and go shop for Saturday's menu. Heading to the town square, where I can pick up groceries and maybe post a note on a board.

parameters.content: Heading to the town square to shop for Saturday's dinner now that dessert is settled.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
